title: Triton multi-region MMA wrongly rejects typed indexed-load operands

evidence.scope: CPU source assessment. The B=2, S=65 unrolled Schedule has two proven sequence K carries but is refused by TRITON_NESTED_MMA_OPERAND. The separately nested batch/sequence source remains a non-K escape. The Executor id identifies the same frozen source; no host or GPU admission was performed for this Finding. Evidence files are retained privately under this logical artifact id.

observation: The existing AccessMap owns a LOAD global source and first-use-ordered unique BUFFER/SCALAR_BUFFER address dependencies. The multi-region MMA preflight assumed one LOAD read and rejected legal indexed load/cast/transpose chains even though the common Schedule analysis already proved their K axes. Dropping the index read would violate ACCESS_INDEX_BUFFER_READS; it is not a valid repair.
proposed_change: Read the unique LOAD AccessMap, require its global source followed by every canonical address dependency, and keep unique writes, typed cast/transpose provenance, producer order, scope and carry checks unchanged. Do not widen the existing loop-nesting domain.
promotion_disposition: A shared Triton admission bug repair is implemented and CPU-verified for exact xcore1002 and gfx938 source routes. No IR primitive, transform pass, target capability or performance claim is added. Independent source review found no blocking issue; integration remains a separate action. Native compilation, device correctness and full original Bench acceptance remain separate.
